title: BATNA (Best Alternative to a Negotiated Agreement)
description: Your best option if no deal is reached. It is your real-world walk-away plan, not a number.

sections.title: What It Is
sections.content: Your best option if no deal is reached. It is your real-world walk-away plan, not a number.

sections.title: How It Actually Appears
content: A job candidate knows she has another written offer at $72,000 and full remote work. She doesn't reveal the number but feels zero desperation.
A salesperson has three other buyers lined up. Her tone is relaxed, she lets the current buyer do most of the talking, and she doesn't chase.

sections.title: Common Phrases
content: I have other options I'm considering.
I'm not in a rush to decide today.
If this doesn't work, that's okay.

sections.title: Warning Signs of a Weak BATNA
content: Conceding before the other side asks.

sections.title: Why It Works
sections.content: A strong alternative reduces dependency. The less you need this specific deal, the more power you hold. Even just mentally clarifying your BATNA reduces anxiety and prevents over-concession.

sections.title: Protection Strategy
sections.content: Before any negotiation, write down your exact BATNA. If you don't have one, create one (e.g., 'I will stay in my current role for three more months while I continue to interview').

sections.title: Real Scenario
sections.content: A freelance designer receives a low-ball offer. She calmly replies, 'I've got two other projects in the pipeline this month, so I'll have to pass on this unless the rate moves closer to my standard.' The client immediately raises the offer.

sections.title: Key Insight
sections.content: You negotiate differently when you genuinely mean 'I'm fine either way.'
